hints: Use the volume of revolution formula $V = \pi \int_0^2 y^2\,dx$.
walkthrough:
Set up the formula for the volume of revolution about the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^2 y^2\,dx = \pi \int_0^2 \left((x^3 + 1)^{1/2}\right)^2\,dx = \pi \int_0^2 (x^3 + 1)\,dx$$

Evaluate the definite integral between the limits $x = 0$ and $x = 2$:
$$V = \pi \left( \left(\frac{2^4}{4} + 2\right) - 0 \right) = \pi (4 + 2) = 6\pi \approx 18.8$$
